title: Incremental Rollout Traffic Sentinel and KPI Log
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight, operational-ready tracker and checklist for incremental feature or model rollouts that need fine-grained traffic gating. Focused on low-latency, cost-sensitive inference workloads (hosted/dedicated/private). Use as the canonical signal surface for go/no-go and fast rollback decisions during the first 48–72 hours of a rollout.

Scope and when to use this doc:
- Any change that affects model serving path: new model version, quantization profile change, KV cache behavior change, routing policy updates, or batching configuration changes.
- Intended for rollouts that ramp traffic in phases (1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100%). Not for trivial UI copy changes.

Quick owner map:
- Release lead: Aisha Patel
- SRE/Oncall lead: Diego Morales
- Serving runtime eng: Rina Kapoor
- Product PM: Samir Bose
- Customer success (if enterprise beta): assigned CS rep

Success metrics (primary):
- Latency: P95 <= 220ms (hosted API) or baseline + 25ms (dedicated)
- Error rate: request-level error rate <= 0.5% and model-level hallucination trigger <= defined baseline (see eval set)
- Traffic economics: cost-per-1k-tokens delta <= +15% vs baseline for same quality slice
- Quality: automated eval pass-rate on canary prompts >= 98% of baseline metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/Custom classifier thresholds)
- KV cache health: prefix hit-rate >= 60% for cacheable workloads after warm-up window

Secondary signals (watchlist):
- CPU/GPU queue depth and tail latencies
- Pod restart rate and OOM events
- Slow downstream dependencies (vector DB queries, auth)
- Customer-facing error types (403/429/500 distribution)

KPI tracker template (record at each ramp step):
- Ramp step: (e.g., 1%, 5%, 20%)
- Start time / End time:
- Requests sampled:
- P50 / P95 / P99 latency (ms):
- Token throughput (tokens/sec):
- Avg cost per 1k tokens (USD):
- Error rate (%):
- Model eval regression score (relative to baseline %):
- KV cache hit-rate (%):
- Observed anomalies (bullet list):
- Action taken / notes:

Readiness gates (must be green to proceed to next traffic phase):
- Gate A (platform): cluster CPU/GPU usage < 70% and no increase in Pod restarts in 30m window
- Gate B (latency): Rolling P95 in last 15m <= target threshold for this ramp (see success metrics)
- Gate C (errors): error rate and user-visible failures under 0.5% with stable distribution
- Gate D (quality): evaluation harness run on sampled production prompts shows no regression > 2% on critical intents
- Gate E (cost): per-token cost delta acceptable to product/finance stakeholders (pre-approved)

Traffic ramp plan (example timeline):
- T0 (Sanity): 1% for 30–60 minutes. Lightweight smoke checks + sanity eval.
- T1 (Early): 5% for 2 hours. Full KPI sampling and SLO checks.
- T2 (Mid): 20% for 4 hours. Extended monitoring, start warming caches for steady-state.
- T3: 50% for 6–12 hours (overnight possible). Cross-team oncall practice.
- T4: 100% when all gates stable for 12+ hours and no quality regressions.

Immediate rollback triggers (auto + manual):
- Auto-rollback: sustained P95 above threshold by >40% for 15m AND error rate increase >200% relative to baseline
- Manual rollback recommended: evidence of model hallucination on customer-sensitive intents, security-related failures, or a critical downstream outage
- Rollback steps: switch routing policy to pinned baseline model variant -> reduce traffic to 0% for variant -> validate recovery -> communicate to stakeholders

Monitoring dashboard checklist (to create / verify before rollout):
- Rolling latency (P50, P95, P99) by region and tier
- Error rate with breakdown by type and endpoint
- Cost telemetry: per-request token counts and per-1k cost estimates
- Quality probes: continuous eval results for a 200-prompt smoke harness derived from customer samples
- Heatmap for KV cache hits by route and prefix length
- Canary logs with request/response sampling (redact PII)

Communication play (who gets pinged and when):
- Phase start: @release-lead + eng oncall + product summary slack channel (#prod-rollouts)
- Auto-rollback: immediate page to SRE + release lead + product, post to runbook channel
- Manual rollback: call (10m) between release lead, SRE lead, product lead, and engineering owner
- Post-mortem: timeline + metrics within 48 hours if rollback occurred or if any gate was marginal

Operational notes / runbook snippets:
- Warm caches before increasing beyond 20%: run warm-up job with representative prefixes for 30m. Record cache hit-rate before ramp.
- Batching policy changes: run a controlled synthetic load test in staging with representative batch size distribution. Tag any kernel/compilation variance.
- Private deployments: ensure KMS/HSM calls are measured — key-agent latency spikes can masquerade as model slowdowns.

Unchecked risks & questions (notes to self):
- Do we have a clear mapping from customer intents -> critical intent list for quality probes? (TODO: Samir to finalize by 2025-01-17)
- Billing impact for sustained 50%: need finance sign-off if cost delta > 10% over 24h (action: product ops request)
- Can oncall script automatically run eval harness and upload results to the dashboard? (Rina prototype: JIRA-PI-789)

Post-launch evaluation checklist (48–72h):
- Aggregate KPI deltas vs baseline at 1h, 6h, 24h, 72h
- Spot-check top 50 user queries for quality regressions and false positives
- Confirm no customer support spike beyond 2x baseline in first 24h
- Update model tag/metadata and archive sampled canary requests (redacted) for future audits

Appendix: quick command snippets for release lead
- Force revert routing policy (CLI): redwood routing set-variant --service chat --variant baseline --traffic 100
- Launch cache warmup job (CLI): redwood ops cache-warm --service chat --prefix-list warm_v1 --duration 30m
- Run local eval harness (run against canary): scripts/eval/run_canary_eval.sh --sample 200 --report out/canary-2025-01-10.json

TODOs before next use:
- Build a compact dashboard template in Console that auto-populates KPI tracker rows for each ramp step (owner: Rina)
- Create a templated Slack playbook message with gated fields for each phase (owner: Diego)
- Finalize critical-intent list and map to evaluation thresholds (owner: Samir)

Notes: draft iteration — use this doc as the operational log during a real rollout. Capture timestamps and paste KPI rows under the KPI tracker template above.
